channel.title: Comments on: A Word to the Wise?
channel.description: taoism, taoist thought, buddha, yoga, tai chi, shakuhachi

item.title: By: Carl
item.dc:creator: Carl
item.description:
As usual Lynn, good question!
You should have seen them when they were younger... from inside their shoes, of course. Younger people will tend to mask their inner nature (needs and fears) by donning a persona that eases their social and economic way through life (e.g., "how to win friends and influence people"). With age, a lot of the motivation for, and dream of , 'making it' subsides as the grave approaches.
Additionally, we are who we are due to genetics and circumstances. That leaves many 'broken individuals' in civilized circumstances (competition, isolation, double standards,...). While everyone, I mean everyone, learns from living life, we don't necessarily learn enough to make it noticeable to the outside, especially when we start out from a hole due to unfavorable circumstances (mostly).
Consider this: a person with Hitler's genome born into a close knit tribe 20,000 years ago would not have had the impact a Hitler of the 20th century had. There are maladjusted individual animals in the wild. That is just part of natural diversity, i.e., maladjusted in one setting can be a huge survival advantage in another setting. There is no 'evil' in nature. From a Taoist point of view, so-called evil is a consequence of language and civilization.
<a href="https://centertao.local/blog/2010/11/22/a-symptoms-point-of-view/" rel="nofollow">Viewed as a symptom</a>, spirituality is a social myth (i.e., <a href="https://centertao.local/tao-te-ching/carl/chapter-65/" rel="nofollow">Of ancients adept in the way, none ever use it to enlighten people. They will use it in order to fool them</a>.) It serves a social purpose, naturally... a hierarchical purpose I'd guess. Spirituality implies free will. Without free will, there can be no spirituality. This means that we truly all do the best we can in life with what we inherit genetically and circumstantially. Of course, that is an unattractive thought for it makes it impossible to blame anyone for anything. And, what would we do with enemies to rally against.

item.title: By: Lynn cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn cornish
item.description:
Why do you think it is that some people never wise up. You certainly have met old people who are mean, closed up, stubborn, paranoid, and hateful. My father was like that.
Why do you suppose some people age like fine wine and others just kind of lay there decomposing? Does it have something to do with intellect? Genetics (oh please no)? Spirituality?
My friend's Mom is 92 and so not wise. She just repeats the same habitual behaviors over and over with no awareness of what she us doing and what distress she causes others.
